# A color's string is its hex(): `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when it is not
# opaque, on every target (Jonathan's call). It reads back as the literal, and
# two different colors print differently.
#
# The interpreter and the fold printed it as the struct it is held as,
# `{r = 51, g = 102, b = 153, a = 255}`; html as JavaScript's String of the
# record, `[object Object]`; and Go as snglcolor's CSS form, `rgba(…)` when
# translucent.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

const folded = "{#336699}"

component page ui.node {
    var opaque = #336699
    var clear = #33669980

    ui.text #shown(value="{opaque} {clear}")
    ui.text #cast(value=string(clear))
    ui.text #lit(value=folded)
}

func testAColorPrintsAsItsHex(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "#336699 #33669980")
    t.assert(c.cast.value == "#33669980")
    t.assert(c.lit.value == "#336699")
}
